newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan investors to spur further dlr rally -dealers.
newsitem.headline: Japan investors to spur further dlr rally -dealers.

text.p: Japanese investors are betting on the dollar going higher and are playing a key role in aiding its rise against their home currency, dealers and fund managers said on Wednesday.
Adding to the bull run, Japan's trust banks and brokerages are increasingly boosting their dollar positions, they said.
"Investors, especially life insurers, were detected buying dollars actively above 118 yen on recent rallies," said Akira Kase, general manager of the forex market section at Marubeni Corp.
Many investors who held back from buying at around 115 yen on the belief that the dollar's rise would be limited at that level are now finally convinced and are joining the buying spree.
Dealers said these investors are now more aggressive about buying dollars to beef up their foreign-currency portfolios, seeking higher returns by investing overseas.

Tomohiro Kawase, director of Nippon Life Insurance's Finance & Investment Planning Office, told Reuters this week that the company will increase its holdings of foreign-currency-denominated securities.

"We are not betting on a scenario of a rapidly weakening yen (from the current level), but taking account of the gap between Japanese and U.S. interest rates, it is unlikely the yen will rapidly appreciate (in the short term)," Kawase said.

The dollar surged to 122.75 yen, its highest level since February 1993, in Tokyo trading on Wednesday, backed by healthy economic fundamentals in the United States and the market's conviction that major nations will tolerate its rise.
The dollar has already appreciated over six percent against the yen from the beginning of the year.
Fund managers said that the dollar's bullish trend would provide a prime environment for Japanese investors.

"We have been expecting a general bullish trend (of the dollar) for a long time...we have not changed that view," said Takashi Itoda, manager of the international fixed income investment division at Dai-Ichi Mutual Life Insurance Co.
In November, Dai-Ichi Life said it would invest 50 to 100 billion yen in foreign bonds in the second half of the current fiscal year, which ends on March 31.
Itoda said that he was not setting a fixed strategy to decide the timing and targets of deals ahead of time.
"We are building up our foreign bond holdings consistently, in line with our plan," Itoda said.
"We have not set any fixed targets, such as places to buy on dips," he said. "We are maintaining a very flexible stance."
But other insurers were more cautious, spooked by the dollar's climb, which they saw as a bit too rapid.
"These insurers may take profits on rallies ahead of the end of the current fiscal year in March," Marubeni's Kase said.

Many Japanese life insurers have just recovered from the nightmare of the early 1990s when their massive foreign bond investment severely battered their profits due to the yen's sharp appreciation at that time.
Hideo Sakaguchi, general manager of the securities investment section at Meji Life Insurance Co, said the recent rise of the dollar has forced the company to take a more cautious stance.
He added that the outlook for the dollar/yen rate was still unclear at the current stage.
"Sharp falls in the domestic stock market may have exaggerated the yen selling," Sakaguchi said. "But we may see a downward correction (of the dollar) before the end of the fiscal year."

Sakaguchi said Meiji was not changing the foreign bond investment plan set in November to invest about 300 billion yen in foreign bonds in the second half of the year, mainly in short- and medium-term issues.
But he said it may not meet its target by the end of the fiscal year, as the dollar may be too expensive to buy.
